ptr-pg.role: PostgreSQL substrate: ledger projection, derived search cache and non-authoritative work state in one database.
ptr-pg.summary: Three schemas per instance (projection, derived, work) built from checksummed migration catalogs. The projector (apply_committed) is the only writer of the projection and verifies the anchor chain on every record; adapters on PgSubstrate store branches, fast-memory journals, search documents, lineage interference, triage policies and metrics in the work and derived schemas. Everything beyond schemas, catalogs, capability parsing, event mapping and metric compilation needs the postgres-backend feature; no production binary links it, only tests and the feature-gated ptr-bench harnesses.

lib.rs.purpose: Crate root: declares modules and re-exports; adapters and the seal key sit behind the postgres-backend feature.

config.rs.purpose: Safe SQL identifiers, the three-schema set made from one prefix, and the connection configuration naming an environment variable.

capability.rs.purpose: Parses server version and installed extensions; refuses a server older than 16 or without pgvector 0.8.

migrate.rs.purpose: Migration catalogs per schema class, with checksums, placeholder rendering, catalog validation and pending-migration planning.

error.rs.purpose: The typed refusal set of the substrate with stable PTR_PG_* codes and no driver types.

event.rs.purpose: Maps one committed ledger event to its lifecycle effect, topic, subject and payload for the projection and its event log.

metric.rs.purpose: Compiles a ptr-analytics metric specification into one query over the work schema.

seal.rs.purpose: Host-held key that tags stored branches with HMAC-SHA-256 and verifies tags in constant time; Debug is redacted.

adapters/mod.rs.purpose: PgSubstrate: loopback-only connect, capability reading, locked migrate, projection rebuild, drop, and driver-error mapping.

adapters/projection.rs.purpose: The projector: applies one committed record per transaction behind the watermark lock, chain-verified, and answers lifecycle reads.

adapters/events.rs.purpose: Reads the projection event log in commit order and keeps per-consumer committed offsets that only move forward.

adapters/branch.rs.purpose: Stores and loads sealed agent branches, their triage log and outcomes in the work schema; a stored branch is only a candidate.

adapters/fastmem.rs.purpose: Fast-memory registrations, write journal and checkpoints in the work schema, stored as exact f32 bit patterns.

adapters/lineage.rs.purpose: Records and loads adapter interference reports; the rest of the lineage catalog has no adapter yet.

adapters/metrics.rs.purpose: Runs a compiled metric query and returns numerator and denominator per group.

adapters/policy.rs.purpose: Records triage policies with their calibration branches and returns adjudicated calibration samples.

adapters/search.rs.purpose: Derived search cache: embedding spaces, documents of live capsule generations, and hybrid lexical plus vector retrieval of candidates.

ptr-observe.role: Typed trace event, sink trait and field-name constants, with an optional adapter to the tracing crate.
ptr-observe.summary: Defines TraceEvent with typed values, the TraceSink trait, a no-op sink, field-name constants, a FlowSignature record and an optional TracingSink. No other crate in the repository depends on it and nothing outside its own tests builds or emits an event.

lib.rs.purpose: Crate root re-exporting the trace types; the tracing adapter is behind the tracing-adapter feature.

error.rs.purpose: Trace failure kinds with stable lowercase codes.

fields.rs.purpose: String constants naming the standard trace fields such as ptr.request_id and error.code.

flow.rs.purpose: A plain record of a request's operators and state transitions; nothing builds or reads it.

macros.rs.purpose: Internal From-impl macro for trace values plus the exported trace_event! builder macro.

trace.rs.purpose: Trace level, typed value, event with ordered fields, the TraceSink trait and a no-op sink.

tracing_adapter.rs.purpose: A sink that forwards each event to the tracing macros at the matching level with selected fields.

ptr-inspect.role: Inspection tree type, an Inspectable trait and a Secret wrapper that never renders its contents.
ptr-inspect.summary: One file: InspectNode, the Inspectable trait and Secret<T>, whose Debug and inspect output are redacted. It is listed as a workspace member but no crate in the repository depends on it.

lib.rs.purpose: Defines the inspection node tree, the Inspectable trait and the redacting Secret wrapper.

ptr-core.role: Placeholder core-model vocabulary: configs, a few small data types and the ActionIr re-export.
ptr-core.summary: Thirteen tiny files of configuration structs and plain data holders (slots, workspace, branch frontier, router decision, verification result) with a handful of one-line helpers, and no model, attention or reasoning implementation. The only item other crates use is action_head::ActionIr, a re-export of the ptr-types type for compatibility; the rest is exercised only by a one-assert smoke test.

lib.rs.purpose: Declares the twelve modules and re-exports PtrCoreConfig.

action_head.rs.purpose: Re-exports ptr_types::ActionIr, the action type runtime and wire crates import from here.

branch_reasoner.rs.purpose: Branch state with probability and a frontier that drops branches below a threshold.

epistemic_workspace.rs.purpose: A list of semantic slots with a step counter and an iterator over live slots.

latent_reasoner.rs.purpose: Reasoning budget levels and a reasoner that only adds the budget's step count to the workspace counter.

model.rs.purpose: Top-level core configuration choosing autoregressive or diffusion family with default sub-configs.

operator_router.rs.purpose: Weighted operators and a router decision that returns the highest-weight operator.

probabilistic_reasoner.rs.purpose: Normalizes non-negative finite scores into probabilities, all default when the sum is zero.

ptr_ar.rs.purpose: Configuration struct for the autoregressive family: layers, context, latent step maximum.

ptr_diff.rs.purpose: Configuration struct for the diffusion family: blocks, canvas slots, denoise steps.

semantic_slots.rs.purpose: Plain data holder for one semantic slot: role, epistemic state, validity, confidence, value and provenance.

typed_attention.rs.purpose: Configuration struct for typed attention: width, heads and bias and mask switches.

verifier_head.rs.purpose: Plain result record: confidence, contradiction score and need for external verification.

ptr-bench.role: Benchmark and experiment binary: micro benchmarks, the in-memory S003 certified-branches harness and feature-gated PostgreSQL experiments.
ptr-bench.summary: The default build runs semdb, mailbox and ledger recovery benchmarks and the S003 experiment, which drives a real PtrRuntime against an independent reference model with five arms, canaries and probes and prints one JSON result line. With the postgres-experiments feature it also runs L003 (fast-memory revocation) and L004 (projection equivalence) against a loopback PostgreSQL server through ptr-pg.

main.rs.purpose: Command dispatcher for the benchmarks and experiments, plus the ledger recovery and crash benchmarks.

experiments/mod.rs.purpose: Declares the experiment modules; the PostgreSQL ones compile only with the postgres-experiments feature.

experiments/json.rs.purpose: Escapes a string as a JSON string for result lines.

experiments/rng.rs.purpose: Seeded SplitMix64 generator with forked streams so every case is reproducible from its seed.

experiments/pg.rs.purpose: Shared server access for the PostgreSQL experiments: fresh substrate instance per case, tagged sessions, commit-fault trigger.

experiments/l003.rs.purpose: L003 harness: checks no revoked input influences a fast-memory readout across revocation, replay, restore or crash.

experiments/l004.rs.purpose: L004 harness: checks the PostgreSQL projection equals runtime replay and refuses foreign or rolled-back histories.

experiments/s003/mod.rs.purpose: S003 entry: runs cases, each with canaries, probes and every arm, a rerun digest check, and prints the result line.

experiments/s003/params.rs.purpose: Preregistered parameters compiled in, and the canonical text of the frozen table that every result echoes.

experiments/s003/workload.rs.purpose: Per-case contention level, genesis state, tasks with durations and scores, and background actor schedule drawn from seeded streams.

experiments/s003/program.rs.purpose: The nine agent programs, run identically against a real Branch view and a reference view, with footprints compared.

experiments/s003/model.rs.purpose: Reference model of semdb values, deltas and lifecycle authority, reimplemented without calling certification code.

experiments/s003/oracle.rs.purpose: Decides from the model alone which hazards a merge would hit and exactly what the runtime must do.

experiments/s003/verifier.rs.purpose: The two deterministic verifiers of the harness grant: domain rules for every change, counter-jump rule for host writes.

experiments/s003/world.rs.purpose: The runtime under test beside the model: predicts, runs and compares every write, merge, background event and replay.

experiments/s003/arms.rs.purpose: The five arms (serial, certified, certified-review, lww, occ) and the tick scheduler that runs a case's tasks.

experiments/s003/canary.rs.purpose: Nine hand-written footprints with known verdicts that make the oracle itself falsifiable.

experiments/s003/probes.rs.purpose: Adversarial probes run on fixture runtimes: double merges, foreign bases, approvals, holds, sealing rules, forged histories.

experiments/s003/metrics.rs.purpose: Hard, coverage and descriptive counters declared by one macro, plus FNV digesting and the merge wall-time histogram.

experiments/s003/scratch.rs.purpose: Private exclusively created temporary directory for durable round trips, removed on drop.

ptr-burn-a0.role: Burn-based research model A0: slot-typed cross-attention with admission masking, router logits and a codebook-bound checkpoint format.
ptr-burn-a0.summary: Separate workspace. PtrA0 embeds raw tokens and typed slots, attends both ways with a validity-derived additive mask, refines slots and pools admitted slots into operator logits; typed inputs only enter through CodeGrid and SlotValues built from ptr-types. Checkpoints are written as a ptr-types header plus the Burn record and refused on codebook, encoding, table-size or architecture drift. It is exercised by its own tests and examples and used as a real fixture by ptr-runtime and ptrctl tests; the main runtime does not link it.

lib.rs.purpose: The PtrA0 model, its configuration, typed code and slot-value containers, admission_bias and the forward pass, plus a plain baseline.

checkpoint.rs.purpose: Saves and loads weights inside a ptr-types checkpoint header with architecture digest, optionally bound to an M002-v5 contract.

m002_v5_contract.rs.purpose: Reads and digests a frozen M002-v5 contract file and verifies a config or training setup against it.

ptr-fuzz.role: cargo-fuzz harness for the Pod wire protocol decoder.
ptr-fuzz.summary: One fuzz target decodes arbitrary bytes as a PodCall and converts any success into a CallFrame to check that the conversion never panics. It has no corpus or other targets in the repository.

fuzz_targets/podwire.rs.purpose: Fuzz target: decode bytes as PodCall and try CallFrame conversion.

flows.title: PostgreSQL projection and work adapters
flows.summary: A host configures, connects, migrates and then feeds committed ledger records to the projector, which is the only writer of the projection; consumers and work-schema adapters read or write around it.

steps.label: PgConfig::resolve_dsn
steps.note: The connection string is read from the environment variable the config names; unset or blank gives MissingDsn, so no secret lives in a config file.

steps.label: SchemaSet::with_prefix and check
steps.note: Projection, derived and work schema names come from one prefix; a hand-composed set or a pg_ prefix is refused so no two instances share a schema.

steps.label: PgSubstrate::connect_with
steps.note: Refuses a bad schema set, a connection string naming several servers, and any target that is not loopback or a Unix socket because no encrypted transport is linked.

steps.label: capabilities then Capabilities::check_supported
steps.note: Reads server_version_num and pg_extension, then refuses a server below 16 or without pgvector 0.8.0; nothing is ever installed.

steps.label: PgSubstrate::migrate under advisory lock
steps.note: A separate session holds pg_try_advisory_lock keyed by the projection schema; each migration commits only after the lock is reconfirmed, else MigrationLockLost.

steps.label: migrate_locked per SchemaClass and Migration::checksum
steps.note: Creates each schema and schema_migration table, plans pending migrations, applies each in its own transaction and records its SHA-256 checksum; drift, a malformed catalog or a newer unknown version is refused. Catalogs hold 2 projection, 1 derived and 16 work migrations.

steps.label: PgSubstrate::apply_committed
steps.note: One committed record per transaction behind a FOR UPDATE watermark row; the anchor is recomputed from the stored one and a mismatch is ForeignHistory, a duplicate is checked against the stored anchor.

steps.label: Write state_entry, live_generation, tombstone, semantic_revision
steps.note: Entries come from ptr_state::projection_entries; a new live generation or tombstone also deletes derived search documents and fast-memory journal writes and checkpoints of the superseded or revoked generation in the same transaction.

steps.label: Insert projection_event, advance watermark, pg_notify
steps.note: The event row, applied anchor and watermark move in the one transaction that commits; the notification fires only on commit.

steps.label: events_after, consumer_offset, commit_consumer
steps.note: Consumers read events above their offset up to the watermark and commit offsets that only move forward and never beyond the watermark; offsets restart at zero after a rebuild.

steps.label: store_branch, record_triage, record_outcome
steps.note: Sealed branches, triage and outcomes go to the work schema; a merged outcome is accepted only when the projection holds the branch's merge key at exactly that commit index.

steps.label: append_write, upsert_document, record_policy, metric
steps.note: Fast-memory writes and search documents are checked against the projection's live_generation row held FOR SHARE and its tombstones; lineage, policy and metrics adapters write or read only work-schema tables.

steps.label: with_branch_seal_key and BranchSealKey::tag
steps.note: With a host-held key, store_branch writes an HMAC-SHA-256 tag of the branch's seal digest and load_branch refuses a missing tag (BranchWithoutSealTag) or a mismatching one (BranchSealMismatch).

steps.label: database() and PgError::code
steps.note: Driver errors cross the boundary only as SQLSTATE plus message (or a connection error), and every refusal has a stable PTR_PG_* code.

flows.title: S003 certified-branches harness
flows.summary: `ptr-bench certified-branches` draws seeded cases, judges the oracle with canaries, runs adversarial probes and every arm over a real runtime beside a reference model, then prints one JSON line and exits 1 if any hard counter is above zero.

steps.label: main dispatches certified-branches
steps.note: Iterations and seed are parsed strictly (a typo stops the run); defaults are 48 cases and seed 17 from params.

steps.label: params::echo and Case::new
steps.note: The preregistered table in config.toml is compiled in and echoed canonically; each case picks a contention level from the groups ladder (4 to 256 groups) and a stream derived from seed and index.

steps.label: Case::genesis, tasks, background
steps.note: Genesis state, 128 tasks of nine program kinds with per-attempt think and review times, and background actor events come from named streams, so all arms see the same inputs.

steps.label: canary::run
steps.note: Nine hand-written footprints each with a known verdict are judged by the oracle; a miss counts canary_misses and a hard failure.

steps.label: probes::run_all
steps.note: Ten probe groups on fresh fixture runtimes (merged twice, foreign base, relied generation, approvals, held merges, host write rules, sealing rules, grants, forged histories, hazards) count a hard counter when the runtime accepts what it must refuse.

steps.label: run_arm for serial plus four arms at 2, 4, 8, 16 agents
steps.note: Serial uses one agent; certified, certified-review, lww and occ each run at every agent count over the same tasks.

steps.label: World::open
steps.note: An agent opens a real ptr_branch Branch on the runtime snapshot, runs its program, seals it, and the same program runs on a reference view; log and footprint must match or a divergence is counted.

steps.label: Simulation::execute tick loop
steps.note: Each tick runs background actors, then due merges through one lane (oldest first, reviews before agent merges), then idle agents open work; refused tasks retry up to 8 attempts.

steps.label: World::merge calls oracle::judge
steps.note: Before the runtime sees a merge, the oracle predicts hazards and the exact outcome from the model alone; certified arms merge through PtrRuntime::merge_branch under triage or reviewed authority.

steps.label: committed, held, refused compare with the prediction
steps.note: Anything the runtime did that the oracle did not predict increments a hard counter (lost updates, phantoms, stale reads, provenance mismatches); the model then follows the journal and full state is compared.

steps.label: settle_lww and settle_occ baselines
steps.note: Last-writer-wins commits the branch overlay as a host write; occ retries only when a declared read changed. Baseline hazards are counted as evidence, not failures.

steps.label: World::round_trips
steps.note: Certifying arms rebuild a runtime from replay, a compacted snapshot and, in every eighth case, a durable file in a scratch directory, and compare each with the live runtime.

steps.label: Rerun of case 0 and result_line
steps.note: Case 0 runs again from the seed and its digest must match, else nondeterminism; the JSON line lists every counter, the merge wall-time histogram, per-arm statistics and hard_failures, and the process exits 1 if hard_failures is above zero.

flows.title: Burn A0 forward pass and checkpoint
flows.summary: Typed slot codes and encoded values are built from ptr-types, the model embeds them, attends with an admission mask and pools admitted slots into operator logits; the weights are saved and loaded inside a ptr-types checkpoint header.

steps.label: CodeGrid::new through Codebook
steps.note: Role and epistemic codes are minted only through the codebook, with the family as a type parameter, so swapping the two grids does not compile.

steps.label: SlotValues::new from SlotVector
steps.note: Values come only from SlotVectors produced by a named SlotEncoding; rows must share slot count, width and encoding version.

steps.label: admission_bias from ValidityMask
steps.note: ValidityMask::attention_bias gives 0.0 for admitted slots and negative infinity otherwise; admission_bias lifts it to a tensor.

steps.label: PtrA0::forward asserts
steps.note: Panics if batch, slot count, codebook version, slot-encoding version or width disagree with the model.

steps.label: Slot embeddings
steps.note: Token, slot-type, epistemic, provenance and confidence embeddings are summed with the slot values; validity is deliberately not part of the sum.

steps.label: Slots attend to raw tokens
steps.note: Cross attention scores get a bounded metadata bias by mode (LegacyScalarV1, FactorizedV2, or computed and zeroed when Off), then softmax and context.

steps.label: Raw tokens attend to slots with admission bias
steps.note: The admission bias is added last, so excluded slots get exactly zero weight; a row admitting nothing gets a finite bias and its context is zeroed to avoid NaN.

steps.label: Latent refinement and router
steps.note: Slots are refined for latent_steps; the router averages over admitted slots only (legacy mean-linear or calibrated cosine) into operator logits returned in PtrA0Output.

steps.label: checkpoint::header and save
steps.note: The header records model name ptr-a0, codebook, slot-encoding version, table sizes read from the weights and an architecture digest, followed by the Burn record bytes; save_bound adds an M002-v5 contract digest.

steps.label: checkpoint::load
steps.note: Reads the header, refuses another model, calls CheckpointHeader::verify for encoding, codebook bytes and the three embedded family sizes, then checks the architecture digest before decoding any weight; unbound format 2 needs an exact legacy opt-in.

steps.label: CheckpointHeader::verify
steps.note: Refuses a moved encoding, unknown or moved codebook, a missing family table or a table not equal to the family's cardinality.

flows.title: ptr-observe trace and flow types
flows.summary: A caller could build a TraceEvent with the macro and hand it to a TraceSink; in the repository only ptr-observe's own tests do. Nothing emits to it and no crate depends on it.

steps.label: Field-name constants
steps.note: Strings such as ptr.request_id, ptr.revision and error.code name the fields an event may carry.

steps.label: trace_event! or TraceEvent::request
steps.note: Builds an event with a level, name and an ordered map of typed values; request() fills request id and revision.

steps.label: TraceSink::emit
steps.note: The trait takes an event and returns Result<(), TraceError>; the provided NoopTraceSink discards everything.

steps.label: TracingSink::emit
steps.note: With the tracing-adapter feature, picks seven known fields and forwards the event to tracing::error, warn, info, debug or trace by level.

steps.label: FlowSignature
steps.note: A record of request, operator names and state transitions; no code builds or consumes it, so it is a declared type only.
